classes.label: Vanguard
classes.description: A durable martial combatant led by Strength, with greater Constitution. Heavy Strike spends stamina for a stronger single blow. All classes retain physical Attack.

coreAction.label: Heavy Strike
coreAction.description: Commit stamina to one forceful physical strike against your combat opponent.

classes.label: Scout
classes.description: A Dexterity-led martial combatant. Precise Strike spends stamina for a measured single blow. This starting kit grants no stealth, dual wielding, critical hits, or stances.

coreAction.label: Precise Strike
coreAction.description: Spend stamina on a carefully directed physical strike. Armor still applies normally.

classes.label: Kindler
classes.description: An Intelligence-led Resonance practitioner. Directed Heat spends mana to concentrate existing heat through a practiced pattern, with finite reach and cost. Physical Attack remains available.

coreAction.label: Directed Heat
coreAction.description: Guide existing thermal energy along a practiced pattern toward one combat opponent. This costly, bounded working does not create energy from nothing or identify Resonance’s source.

locations.name: Bellwold Market Square
locations.description:
Stalls and handcarts crowd the open ground. The smell of baked bread drifts from the east side of the square.

The tower road rises north and South Common lies south. A lane leads west toward the Kindly Roof; Marr’s General Goods is east.

npcs.name: Linnet Reed
npcs.description: A villager crosses the square at an easy pace, glancing between the market stalls and the road to the well.
npcs.activityDescription: walking between the market and shared spaces
npcs.greeting: “I was headed to the well. Or the square. I’ll know when I get there.”

topics.response: “There is always someone to meet between the square and the well. You learn more by walking than by asking for a grand account.”
“The square is busiest early. By noon, half the people have gone off to their work.”
“Seli keeps cloth in use, Aven keeps the grain tally, and Enna writes down what people agree to do. They each know a different part of the village.”
“My family says the bell warned of storms. I heard the account of seventeen people disappearing while it rang, but nobody in my family could tell me why.”

dialogue.prompt: “I was headed to the well. Or the square. I’ll know when I get there.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “I’m Linnet Reed. I run errands around town and usually find someone to talk to along the way.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m carrying a few things between the square and the well. I have not decided which I’ll reach first.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold is small enough that an errand can turn into a conversation, then another errand. I like that about it.”

choices.label: When is the square busiest?
choices.response: “Early, when the stalls are opening. By noon most folk have gone to their own work, and the square belongs to whoever still has an errand.”

choices.label: Who should I ask about the village?
choices.response: “Seli knows cloth, Aven knows the grain tally, and Enna keeps the public notes. Ask each what they can show you; none of us sees the whole town.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I’m just on an errand. Try the market or the well if you need directions.”

narrative.arrival: A villager enters from the {direction}, nodding to a familiar face.
narrative.departure: A villager leaves toward the {direction}, carrying on with a town errand.

npcs.name: Taren Voss
npcs.description: A guard in a weathered coat stands near the square’s edge, scanning the road and nearby crossings.
npcs.activityDescription: watching the square and the road
npcs.greeting: “Keep the road clear and let people pass. That is most of the work.”

topics.response: “My circuit runs from the tower road through the square and down to the Common House. I check each crossing as I go.”
“The north road is quiet most days. I still walk it; quiet is not the same as watched.”
“The Crown of Heskar keeps rigid borders and strong property laws. My patrol keeps crossings clear; it does not decide where Bellwold’s jurisdiction begins.”
“The reports describe different authorities: merchant city-states, mountain assemblies, river councils, and communities beyond centralized rule. I guard this circuit, not the whole continent.”

dialogue.prompt: “Keep the road clear and let people pass. That is most of the work.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Taren Voss. I watch the village roads and crossings.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m making my circuit through the square and the public lanes. I look for trouble before it reaches someone’s door.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold is a working village near a frontier. Most days are quiet, but quiet roads still need watching.”

choices.label: Where does your patrol go?
choices.response: “From the tower road through the square, down to the Common House and Well Court, then back along the public lanes. I check crossings as I go.”

choices.label: What do you hear about places beyond Bellwold?
choices.response: “Reports speak of merchant city-states, mountain assemblies, river councils, and communities with no central ruler. I guard this circuit; I can’t vouch for every report.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I’m on patrol. Keep to the marked paths and speak plainly if there’s trouble.”

narrative.arrival: The guard enters from the {direction}, eyes alert.
narrative.departure: The guard leaves toward the {direction}, continuing the patrol.

npcs.name: Orin Vale
npcs.description: A broad-hatted angler walks with a folded net under one arm, pausing to study the river whenever the road bends near it.
npcs.activityDescription: walking between the market square and the south bridge
npcs.greeting: “The river gives no promises. A patient line and a little luck are all I ever had.”

topics.response: “The current under the south bridge still holds bass, carp, and trout. You need a rod to fish from the bridge.”

dialogue.prompt: Orin turns a worn fishing rod in his hands. “I’ve no use for this old thing now. Would you like it?”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Orin Vale. I have spent more of my life beside the river than I planned to.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I walk between the square and the south bridge, watching the current and checking the line when I can.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold suits me. The river is close, and there is usually someone in the square who will share a word.”

choices.label: What fish live under the bridge?
choices.response: “Smallmouth bass, carp, and trout. The river gives no promise that any one of them will take your line.”

choices.label: Any advice for fishing here?
choices.response: “Watch where the current slows beside the stones. Then be patient. If you rush the line, you’ll only hear the water laugh at you.”

choices.label: Accept the old rod
choices.response: “Here you are. The cork is worn, but the line still holds. Cast from the south bridge and wait for a bite.”

itemReward.label: old rod
itemReward.description: A weathered fishing rod with a worn cork handle and a serviceable length of line.

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I’m headed back toward the bridge. The river is the only thing I know well.”

narrative.arrival: Orin arrives from the {direction}, glancing toward the river.
narrative.departure: Orin heads {direction}, his folded net tucked beneath one arm.

locations.name: The Kindly Roof
locations.description: Firelight warms the common room, and low voices drift between the tables. A trace of smoke clings to the rafters. The market square lies east; a narrow road leaves west.

npcs.name: Tomas
npcs.description: Behind the common-room counter, Tomas turns from one traveler to the next, listening as low voices drift around the tables.
npcs.activityDescription: listening to travelers in the common room
npcs.greeting: “Come in and warm yourself. If you want the road news, ask who saw it and when.”

dailyJobResponses.response: “Thank you for taking the fish notice. Deliver them at the South Common board; there is room in the supper pot.”
“Your fish arrived from the board today. Supper will be better for it—thank you.”
“Thank you for taking the fish notice. Deliver them at the South Common board; there is room in the supper pot.”
“Your fish arrived from the board today. Supper will be better for it—thank you.”
“You are bringing pine logs for the kitchen? Leave them through the South Common board when you are ready.”
“The kitchen has the pine logs you delivered today. That is one less worry before supper. Thank you.”

topics.response: “Check the South Common bulletin board for today’s jobs. Accept and deliver there.”

dailyJobResponses.response: “Thank you for taking the fish notice. Deliver them at the South Common board; there is room in the supper pot.”
“Your fish arrived from the board today. Supper will be better for it—thank you.”
“Thank you for taking the fish notice. Deliver them at the South Common board; there is room in the supper pot.”
“Your fish arrived from the board today. Supper will be better for it—thank you.”
“You are bringing pine logs for the kitchen? Leave them through the South Common board when you are ready.”
“The kitchen has the pine logs you delivered today. That is one less worry before supper. Thank you.”

topics.response: “The tower road leaves from the square. The mill is farther along. I can tell you what travelers report, not what waits for you there.”
“Professor Elira Venn was investigating the old bell and disappeared near Bellwold. I have no reliable account of what happened after.”
“The older account says the bell warned of storms, then rang without stopping while seventeen villagers disappeared. It records the terrible sequence, not its cause.”

“Travelers describe a continent of different arrangements: guild-influenced city-states in Merefall, temple and civic authority in Veyrun, mountain assemblies in Sareth, and negotiated river rights in Rillward. I repeat what they tell me; I have not walked every road myself.”

dialogue.prompt: “Come in and warm yourself. If you want the road news, ask who saw it and when.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Tomas. I keep the rooms and common table at the Kindly Roof.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m tending the inn and listening for travelers’ news. I try to keep what I hear separate from what I know.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold is a place where the roads bring fresh faces through, but most of the work is still done by the people who live here.”

choices.label: What do travelers say about the wider world?
choices.response: “Different things, depending on which road they came by. I can repeat their accounts, but I haven’t walked those places myself.”

choices.label: What happened to Professor Venn?
choices.response: “She was studying the old bell, then disappeared near Bellwold. I’ve heard no reliable account of what happened after. I won’t dress a gap in the story as an answer.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I keep rooms and hear travelers. I don’t claim to know every answer.”

locations.name: Bellwold West Gate
locations.description: The western lane passes the last village fences and a simple timber gate. The Kindly Roof is east; the westbound road runs past the hedgerows.

locations.name: Westbound Track
locations.description: The packed-earth road follows low hedgerows beyond Bellwold’s western fields. The West Gate is east; the rough road end is west.

locations.name: Western Road Verge
locations.description: The packed track narrows between scrub and open ground. A rutted farm road carries on west beside a drainage ditch toward Harrowfen’s fields; West Gate lies back to the east.

locations.name: Harrowfen Road Ditch
locations.description: The farm road runs beside a straight drainage ditch. Cart wheels have cut the bank, and the mud near the reeds is churned by something heavier. Flat fields open to the west; the Western Road Verge is east.

locations.name: East Field Gate
locations.description: A field gate stands open where the road meets Harrowfen’s first strips of grain and flax. Low fields stretch away under a wide sky. The threshing green is west; the road back to Bellwold runs east.

locations.name: Threshing Green
locations.description: A beaten circle of shared ground is swept clear for threshing, with flails stacked against a post. The weigh-house is north, a drainage cut runs south, and the tenant cottages line the way west. The field gate is east.

locations.name: Weigh-House
locations.description: A squat timber house holds a heavy beam scale and a board of chalked tallies. Sacks wait by the door to be weighed. The threshing green is south.

readables.label: Yield tallies
readables.description: A board of chalked columns beside the beam scale.
readables.text: The columns record seed sown, the weather and the sacks weighed, season by season. The recent columns are shorter than the older ones, though the weather notes for those seasons read “fair” and “good”. A line at the foot asks next season’s tellers to note which field each load came from. The tallies do not say why the yields have fallen.

npcs.name: Reeve Maela Thorn
npcs.description: Maela Thorn stands by the beam scale with a stub of chalk, comparing this season’s sacks against last year’s marks.
npcs.activityDescription: checking sacks against the tallies
npcs.greeting: “If you’ve come about the fields, tell me what you’ve seen. I’ve heard plenty of guesses already.”

topics.response: “Yields are down, and the weather’s been fair. Some blame tired soil, some the drainage, some Resonance. I don’t know yet, and I won’t pretend to.”
“Most of these fields belong to noble families. Tenants, hired hands and smallholders do the work, and they don’t all want the same thing from me.”
“The village chose me to speak for the farmers. That gives me a voice with the landholders. It doesn’t give me their deeds.”

“Someone has offered cheap grain if we let them set up a Veyl extraction operation here. Some want the food and the work. Others ask who would consent, and what it would cost the land. Nobody has shown me what it would really do.”
“Our food and flax go toward Bellwold, and plenty more moves on through Rillford. When a season is short, everyone down the road feels it.”
“We’ve no forge here. A broken share goes to whoever can mend it, and the fields wait.”

dialogue.prompt: “If you’ve come about the fields, tell me what you’ve seen. I’ve heard plenty of guesses already.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Maela Thorn, reeve of Harrowfen. I worked these fields before the village chose me to speak for the people who farm them.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m checking this season’s sacks against last year’s marks. The numbers keep coming up short.”

choices.label: What is Harrowfen like?
choices.response: “A hundred fields and a lot of opinions. The land mostly belongs to noble families; the work belongs to everyone else.”

choices.label: Why are the harvests falling?
choices.response: “I don’t know. Tired soil, the drainage, Resonance: I’ve heard them all. Until we keep better field records, they’re guesses.”

choices.label: What is this offer of cheap grain?
choices.response: “Cheap grain in exchange for letting someone set up a Veyl extraction operation. It would feed people this year. Nobody can tell me what it would do after that.”

choices.label: Publish a conversion table
choices.response: “A public table would let both towns check the next handoff without pretending the two scales are the same. I’ll try it with the next load.”

choices.label: Record both measures side by side
choices.response: “Keeping both marks visible would make the difference plain at each handoff. I’ll use that record for the next load.”

choices.label: Report the measure recommendation
choices.response: “I’ve entered the method beside the tallies. You kept the records separate from any guess about the harvest.”

questResponses.response: “The tallies are here. Read Anwen Marr’s scale note in Bellwold too; these records do not explain why the yields fell.”
“I still need my yield tallies read alongside Anwen’s scale note. Then we can decide how to record a future load.”
“We have both records now. Ask what Harrowfen is like, then tell me which method you recommend for the next grain handoff.”
“The next load will use a public conversion table. That gives both towns a way to check the handoff; it does not explain the falling yields.”
“The next load will record both measures side by side. The difference will stay visible, though its cause remains unknown.”
“The recommendation is entered with the tallies. We still need more seasons of careful records to understand the harvest.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Ask me about the fields, the harvest or the people who work them.”

locations.name: Drainage Cut
locations.description: A long channel drains the low fields. Its sides are freshly recut in places and slumped in others, as if no two seasons agreed on how the water should run. The threshing green is north.

locations.name: Tenant Row
locations.description: Small cottages face the lane, each with a patched roof and tools hung by the door. The people who work the fields live here; most of the land beyond belongs to others. The threshing green is east and the west fields lie beyond.

locations.name: West Fields
locations.description: Strips of grain, root crops and flax run toward the horizon, divided by ditches and a weathered boundary stone carved with an estate mark. Tenant Row is east.

locations.name: Marr’s General Goods
locations.description: Provision jars line the shelves. Near the counter, a balance scale sits beside an open ledger; a brass weight glints in the window light.

readables.label: Scale note
readables.description: A short note beside the balance scale.
readables.text: Anwen has recorded several measurements that do not agree with the weights placed on the scale. She has not decided whether the fault is in the instrument, its surroundings, or the way it is being read.

takeables.label: Bronze Axe
takeables.description: A serviceable bronze axe for woodcutters of level 1 or higher, left near the counter for travelers who need to cut their own firewood.

npcs.name: Anwen Marr
npcs.description: A brass weight rests in Anwen Marr’s palm as she studies the balance scale and makes a note in an open ledger.
npcs.activityDescription: checking a measure beside her ledger
npcs.greeting: “Welcome to my shop. If you want to understand a thing, start with what it does—not with what you hope it means.”

topics.response: “People call this the Age of Measures. Scholars are testing the physical world and Resonance with instruments. A repeatable result matters, but it still does not explain itself.”
“The readings are repeatable often enough to trouble me. That does not tell us what causes them.”
“A sprite is one possibility people raise. It is not an answer I can prove.”
“The bell fell silent while Professor Venn was measuring it. The order of events is known; the cause is not.”
“Heskar has strict property law and guarded borders. Bellwold is near that frontier; the records I have seen do not settle the village’s exact legal status.”

dialogue.prompt: Anwen sets her pencil beside the ledger. “What would you like to ask?”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Anwen Marr. I run this shop and keep notes on measurements that do not quite add up.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m checking a scale against its weights and recording the readings before I draw any conclusions.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold gets by on practical exchange. That makes honest measures and clear records important, even when they raise more questions.”

choices.label: What do the scale readings tell you?
choices.response: “They repeat often enough to deserve attention. That tells me the pattern is real; it does not tell me what causes it.”

choices.label: Ask about the watermill
choices.response: “The mill has been abandoned, but there are reports of its wheel moving when the channel is low. There is a ledger inside. Would you read the last entries and bring me what they actually say?”

choices.label: Ask about the abandoned church
choices.response: “There is a locked annex beneath the abandoned church. A brass key is behind the tally cabinet in the Old Grain House. A sword is sealed beyond that door. Bring it to me; I will pay you 20 gold, inspect the blade, and return it to you.”

choices.label: Report what the ledger says
choices.response: “Good. Keep the record separate from the explanation. One tells us what was observed; the other still needs work.”

choices.label: Return the church sword
choices.response: “Anwen checks the blade and its fittings, then places the same sword back in your hands. She counts out 20 gold. ‘Keep it. You found it, and now it is accounted for.’”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I’m working. Ask plainly, and I’ll answer if I know.”

item.label: Iron Axe
item.description: A balanced iron axe. Requires Woodcutting level 10.

item.label: Steel Axe
item.description: A keen steel axe. Requires Woodcutting level 20.

item.label: Crafting Needle
item.description: A small, reusable needle for stitching leather at a workbench.

item.label: Spool of Thread
item.description: A tightly wound spool of strong thread, with five uses.

locations.name: Bellwold South Common
locations.description: Benches stand beside drying lines and a bulletin board. Voices and footsteps carry across the grass. The market square is north, the Green Mortar west, Blackwater Forge east, and Well Court south.

readables.label: Bulletin board
readables.description: A broad plank board holds handwritten notices in uneven rows.
readables.text: Residents post daily jobs and requests here. Read the bulletin to see current postings and rewards. Accept a posting, then follow its instructions to complete it. New postings appear with each daily refresh.

locations.name: The Green Mortar
locations.description: Bundles of dried plants hang above a workbench; clean cloth is folded near a shallow bowl. The sharp scent of crushed herbs lingers in the air. The open green is east; Wattle Row is south.

npcs.name: Ilya Fen
npcs.description: Ilya sorts dried leaves into shallow trays beside a bowl and a stack of folded cloth.
npcs.activityDescription: sorting plants at her workbench
npcs.greeting: “Tell me what you noticed and when. A careful account is a better beginning than a guess.”

topics.response: “Rest, clean water, and a clear description of what changed can matter as much as any remedy. I will not promise more than I know.”
“I gather what grows nearby, but a plant’s reputation is not proof of what it can do.”
“The Sareth Cantons are known for universities, but not every healer studies in one. Much care is taught by practice, observation, and an experienced hand.”
“Researchers are testing plant, mineral, and cooperative approaches to healing. They are promising in some cases, but costly and not yet easy to provide everywhere.”

dialogue.prompt: “Tell me what you noticed and when. A careful account is a better beginning than a guess.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Ilya Fen. I tend this workroom and help with the ordinary aches and cuts people bring through the door.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m sorting plants and preparing clean cloth. I keep track of what I have actually tried.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold is neighborly in a practical way. People bring one another news, herbs, and a hand when work piles up.”

choices.label: How do you know which herbs help?
choices.response: “I keep notes on what I have used and what changed. A plant’s reputation is not proof, so I won’t promise more than I have seen.”

choices.label: What are healers trying elsewhere?
choices.response: “I hear researchers are testing plant, mineral, and cooperative approaches that use less Essence. Some results sound promising, but they are costly and still uncertain.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I can speak about the care I have seen here. Ask me something specific.”

locations.name: Blackwater Forge
locations.description: Tongs and hammers hang over a dark stone hearth. Half-mended iron pieces rest on the bench, and coal smoke clings to the beams. South Common lies west.

npcs.name: Darric Holt
npcs.description: Darric turns a half-mended iron fitting beside the forge, coal smoke darkening the sleeve of his work shirt.
npcs.activityDescription: repairing a farm fitting at the forge
npcs.greeting: “If something is broken, show me where it failed. If it is only a rumor, I have work to finish.”

dailyJobResponses.response: “You took the pine-log job. Good. Deliver the logs at the South Common board when you have enough.”
“Your pine logs came through today. Useful work for the forge. Thank you.”

topics.response: “Check the South Common bulletin board for today’s jobs. Accept and deliver there.”

dailyJobResponses.response: “You took the pine-log job. Good. Deliver the logs at the South Common board when you have enough.”
“Your pine logs came through today. Useful work for the forge. Thank you.”

topics.response: “Most days it is hinges, blades, and cart fittings. Keeping a place working is less dramatic than building it from scratch.”
“I know how metal wears. I do not know why the tower bell went silent.”
“Some people speak of creation as a workshop shaped by seven artisans. I understand the metaphor; it does not tell me which faith is right, or why the bell went quiet.”
“A boundary mark can matter as much as a fence under Heskar law. A smith can mend the hinge; settling the claim is someone else’s work.”

dialogue.prompt: “If something is broken, show me where it failed. If it is only a rumor, I have work to finish.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Darric Holt. I mend tools, hinges, blades, and whatever else survives the forge.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m repairing a farm fitting. It is easier to find the fault while the metal is still warm.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold holds together because people repair what they have. New work matters, but so does keeping a gate on its hinges.”

choices.label: What do you know about the silent bell?
choices.response: “I know how metal wears. I don’t know why that bell fell silent while Professor Venn was measuring it.”

choices.label: What is the Sevenfold Workshop?
choices.response: “Some tell creation as a workshop shaped by seven artisans. It is a story about craft, not an answer to every question about the world.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Ask about the work here. I am not a keeper of every local story.”

locations.name: Bellwold Well Court
locations.description:
A stone-rimmed well and a broad trough give this quiet court a steady rhythm of buckets, footsteps, and short conversations. A covered storehouse stands to the east; Wattle Row branches west.

South Common is north, and the Common House is south.

locations.name: Wattle Row
locations.description: Low homes and work yards line a narrow lane. Pale new strips weave through the older, darkened reeds of the wattle walls. The Green Mortar is north, Well Court east, a wheelwright’s yard west, and Tallow End Cottage south.

locations.name: Soven’s Wheelwright Yard
locations.description: A turning frame, wooden spokes, and a rack of finished rims fill this fenced yard. Shavings gather in the corners despite the broom leaning by the gate; the sound of a saw carries from the south.

npcs.name: Rell Soven
npcs.description: Rell turns a cart wheel by its rim, pausing to watch it wobble against the wooden frame.
npcs.activityDescription: checking a cart axle
npcs.greeting: “A wheel tells you where it is failing if you watch it turn.”

topics.response: “I make the parts that keep a cart straight on a rough road. Most repairs begin with listening for a wobble.”
“I have not worked on the mill wheel. I can describe a wheel; I cannot say what moves one when no one is there.”
“A cart takes the road it can pass. In the river settlements, access is negotiated with councils; in Merefall, guilds shape much of the trade. The route depends on who has agreed to carry what.”

dialogue.prompt: “A wheel tells you where it is failing if you watch it turn.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Rell Soven. My family has made and mended wheels here for as long as I can remember.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m checking a cart wheel for a wobble before I fit it back to the axle.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold’s lanes are rough on carts. That keeps my yard busy, and it means the village can keep moving its goods.”

choices.label: Have you worked on the old mill wheel?
choices.response: “No. I can tell you what a wheel should sound like, but I haven’t inspected that one. I won’t pretend a familiar shape explains why it might move.”

choices.label: How do goods travel beyond Bellwold?
choices.response: “By whatever route can carry them. I hear river communities negotiate access together, while guilds shape a lot of trade in Merefall.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Ask me about wheels or the work in this yard.”

locations.name: Tallow End Cottage
locations.description:
A narrow cottage opens onto Wattle Row. A loom stands beside the window, with folded cloth kept clear of the hearth and a basket of mending beside the door.

Wattle Row is north; the Common House is east.

npcs.name: Seli Tor
npcs.description: Seli draws a pale thread taut through a strip of cloth at the loom by the window.
npcs.activityDescription: weaving cloth at her loom
npcs.greeting: “Mind the loose thread by the door. It has already caught two sleeves today.”

dailyJobResponses.response: “You took my hide notice? Bring the hides to the South Common board when you have them. I have the torn seams ready.”
“Those hides you delivered today will mend a good few seams. Thank you for seeing to my notice.”
“You took my hide notice? Bring the hides to the South Common board when you have them. I have the torn seams ready.”
“Those hides you delivered today will mend a good few seams. Thank you for seeing to my notice.”

“You took my hide notice? Bring the hides to the South Common board when you have them. I have the torn seams ready.”
“Those hides you delivered today will mend a good few seams. Thank you for seeing to my notice.”

topics.response: “A torn sack is a small problem until the road is long. Most of my work keeps ordinary things useful a little longer.”
“The lane is close, but people keep their own hours. You learn who is awake by the sound of their work.”
“People passing through carry different ways of wrapping, mending, and marking their things. I ask what a pattern means before I assume it belongs to a faith or a family.”

dialogue.prompt: “Mind the loose thread by the door. It has already caught two sleeves today.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Seli Tor. I weave cloth and mend the things people need to carry or wear.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m working a length of cloth at the loom. If I stop halfway through, I lose the line.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold’s lanes are close, so people notice one another’s work. Most neighbors are willing to lend a hand when it is needed.”

choices.label: What is Wattle Row like?
choices.response: “Close-set doors and everyone keeping their own hours. You can usually tell who is awake by the sound of their work.”

choices.label: What do travelers teach you about cloth?
choices.response: “They bring different ways to wrap, mend, and mark their belongings. I ask what a pattern means before I decide it belongs to a family or a faith.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I am happy to talk, but the loom will not wait forever.”

locations.name: Old Grain House
locations.description: A timber storehouse stands on a raised stone sill; narrow vent gaps cut the upper walls. Chalk marks cross the faces of several storage bins. Well Court is west.

takeables.label: Old church key
takeables.description: A tarnished brass key with a long, worn bit. It fits the iron door beneath the abandoned church.
takeables.roomDescription: A tarnished brass key lies behind the grain tally cabinet.

npcs.name: Aven Rusk
npcs.description: Aven checks the chalk marks on a grain bin, then writes in a narrow ledger.
npcs.activityDescription: checking the grain tally
npcs.greeting: “If you need the store, tell me what you are looking for. I keep the tally, not the harvest.”

topics.response: “The chalk marks sort the bins by season, not by owner. I update them when stores are checked; they do not tell us what next season will bring.”

“Other places keep different accounts. I hear that guilds weigh heavily on commerce in Merefall, while Rillward communities record agreements over river access. My own tally only speaks for this store.”
“I write down what comes in and what leaves. A neat ledger is useful, but it cannot explain every loss.”

dialogue.prompt: “If you need the store, tell me what you are looking for. I keep the tally, not the harvest.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Aven Rusk. I keep the grain store’s tally and check what comes in and goes out.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m comparing the chalk marks on these bins with the ledger before I update the count.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold shares stores when it has to. Clear records help us know what is here without pretending to predict what comes next.”

choices.label: How do you keep the grain tally?
choices.response: “The chalk marks sort bins by season, not by owner. I record what comes in and what leaves; the tally cannot tell me what next season will bring.”

choices.label: Do other places keep different records?
choices.response: “That is what I hear. Guilds weigh heavily on accounts in Merefall; along the Rillward rivers, communities record agreements about access.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Ask about the storehouse or its records, and I will check what I know.”

locations.name: Bellwold Common House
locations.description: A long timber room holds a scuffed table and mismatched benches. Paper notices cover one wall, and fresh ink smells sharp near the record book. Well Court is north, Tallow End Cottage is west, and the south road leaves town beyond the last yards.

npcs.name: Enna Pell
npcs.description: Enna bends over an open record book, copying a line from one of the notices on the wall.
npcs.activityDescription: copying a notice into the village record book
npcs.greeting: “The notes are public. If something is missing, tell me what you saw and when.”

topics.response: “People bring repairs, water use, and market-day concerns here. The notes record what was agreed, not what everyone wished had been agreed.”
“I keep the wording close to what people said. A record should help the next person check, not decide for them.”
“One surviving account says the bell rang continuously while seventeen villagers disappeared. It does not give a cause, and I will not add one to the minutes.”
“Our public book records decisions and shared work, not a complete founding story. Bellwold lies near Heskar’s frontier, but these minutes do not establish the village’s legal status.”

dialogue.prompt: “The notes are public. If something is missing, tell me what you saw and when.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Enna Pell. I keep the Common House records and copy notices people bring in.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m writing down the wording of a public notice so the next meeting can check it.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold is held together by small agreements. I try to record what people actually decided, not what I think they meant.”

choices.label: What gets discussed at the Common House?
choices.response: “Repairs, water use, and market-day concerns. The notes record what was agreed, not what everyone hoped would be agreed.”

choices.label: What do the records say about the old bell?
choices.response: “One account says it rang without stopping while seventeen villagers disappeared. It gives no cause, and I won’t write one into the minutes.”

choices.label: Ask about the grain records
choices.response: “Anwen’s scale note is in her Bellwold shop; Maela keeps Harrowfen’s yield tallies. Read both, then ask Maela how she wants the next handoff recorded. The records do not prove why yields have fallen.”

questResponses.response: “Read Anwen’s scale note and Maela’s yield tallies, then keep each record’s limits clear. The notes show what was measured, not why the harvest changed.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Ask about the public notices or the records kept here.”

locations.name: Bellwold South Gate
locations.description: The last cluster of village yards gives way to a low gate and a packed-earth road. The Common House is north; the southbound track continues south.

locations.name: Hearth Alley
locations.description: Close-set walls cast a narrow strip of shade across the lane. A cooking fire crackles behind one shutter.

locations.name: Lantern Court
locations.description: A dented iron lantern hangs above the lane, and rainwater darkens the stones beneath it.

locations.name: Nettlemere House
locations.description: A copper kettle rattles softly above the hearth, and the kitchen smells of warm bread.

npcs.name: Sella Nettlemere
npcs.description: Sella kneads a small round of dough on the kitchen table, flour dusting her sleeves.
npcs.activityDescription: kneading dough at the kitchen table
npcs.greeting: “Come in out of the lane. Just mind the kettle.”

topics.response: “The lane is narrow, but everyone knows whose door to knock on when a roof leaks or a pot goes missing.”
“The market brings flour through town, but people still trade favors and whatever their own gardens produce.”

dialogue.prompt: “Come in out of the lane. Just mind the kettle.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Sella Nettlemere. I keep this house and bake when there is flour to spare.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m kneading a little dough and keeping an ear on the kettle. It tends to complain before it boils over.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold is a place where a warm loaf can bring half the lane to the door. People share what they can.”

choices.label: What do people eat around here?
choices.response: “Flour comes through the market, and folks add what their gardens have. More often than not, someone brings a dish because a neighbor needs help.”

choices.label: Do you know the people on this lane?
choices.response: “Well enough to know whose door to knock on when a roof leaks or a pot goes missing. We manage to return most things.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I can tell you about this lane, if that’s what you came to ask.”

locations.name: Upper Row House
locations.description: A handloom clicks beside a sunlit window. Wool fibers cling to the rough boards.

npcs.name: Tovin Ashdown
npcs.description: Tovin works a shuttle through the loom, pausing to smooth a loose thread.
npcs.activityDescription: weaving at a handloom
npcs.greeting: “If you’re here about the cloth, give me a moment to finish this row.”

topics.response: “A good length of cloth takes time. Most of mine goes to mending clothes and covering goods before they travel.”
“These lanes grew where people needed a door close to their work. They don’t all lead somewhere grand.”

dialogue.prompt: “If you’re here about the cloth, give me a moment to finish this row.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Tovin Ashdown. I weave cloth here and patch it when it wears through.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m working the shuttle across the loom. I need to finish this row before I can check the loose thread.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold’s houses grew around the jobs people had to do. The lanes are practical, even if they can be hard to navigate at first.”

choices.label: What do you make with the cloth?
choices.response: “Mostly repairs: clothes, sacks, and covers for goods on the road. A sturdy patch can save someone a long walk back to town.”

choices.label: Why are the lanes laid out this way?
choices.response: “People put doors close to their work. The paths followed those needs, not some grand plan, so a few turns lead nowhere special.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Ask me about the loom or the people on this row.”

locations.name: Lower Row
locations.description: A loose shutter taps in the breeze; damp earth darkens the packed lane.

locations.name: Lower Row House
locations.description: A saw scrapes across a plank, scattering pale curls over the workbench.

npcs.name: Renna Kell
npcs.description: Renna trims a warped board against the workbench, then checks its edge with her thumb.
npcs.activityDescription: smoothing a board at the workbench
npcs.greeting: “Close the door behind you; the sawdust gets everywhere.”

topics.response: “A loose step or a split shutter is usually easier to mend before the next rain.”
“The row is quiet until someone starts fixing something. Then the whole lane has an opinion.”

dialogue.prompt: “Close the door behind you; the sawdust gets everywhere.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Renna Kell. I mend boards, shutters, and the small things that keep a house dry.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m trimming a warped plank so it will sit straight against the frame.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold’s lower lanes are full of people fixing one another’s roofs and doors. A good board is worth more than a grand promise.”

choices.label: What do people ask you to repair?
choices.response: “Loose steps and split shutters, mostly. Best to mend them before the next rain makes a small fault expensive.”

choices.label: What is Lower Row like?
choices.response: “Quiet until someone starts fixing something. Then the whole lane has an opinion, and someone usually brings a second pair of hands.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “If it’s about wood or the lane, ask directly.”

locations.name: South Lower Row
locations.description: Packed earth gives way to a patch of worn stone. A dog barks behind a fence.

locations.name: South Lane Cottage
locations.description: A clay pot of thyme sits on the sill; its sharp scent reaches through the open window.

npcs.name: Pella Wren
npcs.description: Pella sorts fresh thyme into a shallow basket beside the window.
npcs.activityDescription: sorting herbs beside the window
npcs.greeting: “There’s enough room by the table if you need to sit.”

topics.response: “I keep a few useful plants close by. I know what I have tried myself, and I leave the rest to people with better notes.”
“People here borrow tools, return them late, and argue about whose turn it is to mend the fence. Then they help anyway.”

dialogue.prompt: “There’s enough room by the table if you need to sit.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Pella Wren. I grow herbs in pots and trade what I can spare.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m sorting thyme for drying. It keeps its scent better if I handle it gently.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold has room for little gardens between the houses. People trade cuttings and stories over the fence.”

choices.label: What grows in your pots?
choices.response: “Thyme, mostly, and a few other useful plants. I’ll tell you what I’ve tried myself; the rest I leave to better notes.”

choices.label: What is daily life like in Bellwold?
choices.response: “Someone borrows a tool, forgets to return it, then helps mend the fence anyway. It’s not grand, but it works.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I can tell you what grows in my pots, or what I’ve seen on the lane.”

locations.name: Bellwold Jail
locations.description: Iron bars cast thin shadows across the stone floor. Keys clink briefly behind the desk.

npcs.name: Sergeant Nera Vail
npcs.description: Sergeant Vail sits behind the desk, turning a key ring over in one hand.
npcs.activityDescription: checking the jail keys
npcs.greeting: “If you have a concern, state what happened and when. I keep the record plain.”

topics.response: “The cell is for keeping people safely while a matter is heard. It is not a sentence, and I do not decide a dispute without a record.”
“Taren walks the public routes. I keep this room and its keys; the two jobs overlap only when someone needs help.”
“I write down what each person says and who witnessed it. A written claim is not the same thing as a proven one.”

dialogue.prompt: “If you have a concern, state what happened and when. I keep the record plain.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Sergeant Nera Vail. I oversee this jail and keep its records.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m checking the keys and making sure the holding cell is in order.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold needs a watch, but a claim is not proof. I keep the record clear and let the facts speak for themselves.”

choices.label: What is the holding cell for?
choices.response: “To keep someone safe while a matter is heard. It is not a sentence, and I don’t decide a dispute without a record.”

choices.label: Who watches the streets?
choices.response: “Taren covers the public routes. I keep this room and its keys. The jobs overlap when someone needs help, but they aren’t the same.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Keep your account specific. I can’t act on a story with no place or time attached.”

locations.name: Jail Holding Cell
locations.description: A narrow barred door stands across from the stone wall. Damp straw smells sour in the close air.

locations.name: Bellwold Library
locations.description: Books and stitched pamphlets fill the shelves around a broad reading table. Dry paper and lamp oil mingle in the air.

readables.label: Shelf guide
readables.description: A hand-lettered guide fixed to the end of a bookcase.
readables.text: “Village notices and copied minutes: left shelf. Field and mill accounts: center shelves. Travel records and maps: right shelf. Ask before removing a bound volume.”

npcs.name: Mira Dell
npcs.description: Mira straightens a stack of stitched booklets, then brushes dust from the table.
npcs.activityDescription: sorting pamphlets at the reading table
npcs.greeting: “The shelves are open. If you need a particular record, tell me what it concerns.”

topics.response: “Most of these are copies or working notes. I keep the source with the copy when I can, so readers know what they are looking at.”
“The room behind this one holds objects residents have lent or found nearby. Their labels say what is known—and leave blank what is not.”
“There is no complete town chronicle here. We have notices, tallies, and pieces of older accounts. They do not all answer the same questions.”

dialogue.prompt: “The shelves are open. If you need a particular record, tell me what it concerns.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Mira Dell. I care for the library and help readers find the records they need.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m sorting pamphlets and putting the copied records back where readers can find them.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold’s past is scattered across notes, tallies, and people’s memories. This library keeps the pieces available without pretending they make one complete story.”

choices.label: Where should I look for a record?
choices.response: “Notices and minutes are on the left, field and mill accounts in the center, and travel records and maps on the right. Ask before taking a bound volume.”

choices.label: What is kept in the museum?
choices.response: “Objects residents lent or found nearby. The labels tell you what is known about each one, and leave the uncertain parts open.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Tell me what you are trying to find. I may know which shelf to check.”

locations.name: Upper Reading Room
locations.description: A long window fills the sloped room with pale light. Pages rustle softly in the draft.

locations.name: Bellwold Local Museum
locations.description: Glass-fronted cases stand against the walls. A slate tally board and a faded waterwheel sketch sit beneath a dusty window.

readables.label: Tally board label
readables.description: A paper label beneath a slate board marked with columns of old chalk lines.
readables.text: “Loaned from the Old Grain House. The surviving marks show measured grain totals; the board’s maker and the dates of the entries are not recorded.”

readables.label: Mill sketch label
readables.description: A paper label beneath a faded drawing of a waterwheel.
readables.text: “Copied from a page kept at the abandoned watermill. The drawing records a wheel and channel but gives no date or account of who made it.”

locations.name: Southbound Track
locations.description:
Wind stirs the grass as Bellwold’s roofs recede north; deer prints mark the softer earth.

The South Gate is north; the reedbed approach lies south.

locations.name: Reedbed Approach
locations.description:
Damp grass brushes the road’s edges, and reeds rustle along the riverbanks. The current deepens toward the stone bridge to the south, and a towpath follows the north bank west toward Rillford.

The Southbound Track is north; Lower Rill Bridge is south.

locations.name: Lower Rill Bridge
locations.description: A low stone bridge carries the south road over the Lower Rill. The current runs east and west beneath its arches. Reedbed Approach is north; Far Bank Track is south.

states.name: Under Lower Rill Bridge
states.description: The river moves beneath the stone arches. The road bridge rumbles overhead as the current passes east and west.

locations.name: West Reach
locations.description: The current passes the bridge piers and slides west beneath the reeds. The bridge lies east; Willow Reach is west.

locations.name: Willow Reach
locations.description: Willow roots trail into the slow water along this stretch. West Reach is east; Far West Reach is west.

locations.name: Far West Reach
locations.description: The river broadens beyond the western reedbeds. Willow Reach is east; Reed Reach is west.

locations.name: East Reach
locations.description: The current emerges from beneath the bridge and runs east through reeds and shallow stones. The bridge lies west; Alder Reach is east.

locations.name: Alder Reach
locations.description: A line of alder trees shadows this stretch of water. East Reach is west; Far East Reach is east.

locations.name: Far East Reach
locations.description: The eastern current continues past the last visible bank and around a long bend. Alder Reach is west.

locations.name: Reed Reach
locations.description: Tall reeds crowd both banks and lean over the slow water. A towpath shows along the north bank. Far West Reach is east; Towpath Reach is west.

locations.name: Towpath Reach
locations.description: The river runs close beside the towpath here, and rope-worn posts stand along the north bank. Reed Reach is east; Rillford’s ferry stage lies west.

locations.name: Ferry Stage
locations.description: A timber stage reaches out over the Lower Rill on tarred piles. Boats tie up along its edge to load and unload, and crews keep an eye on the current while they work. Rillford’s south landing lies across the water; passage over is arranged with the boat crews, and none is taking passengers now. The north quay is north.

states.name: Beside the Ferry Stage
states.description: The current pulls past the tarred piles of Rillford’s ferry stage. Towpath Reach is east; the river runs on west.

readables.label: Crew slate
readables.description: A slate nailed to one of the piles, chalked over in several hands.
readables.text: Crews leave notices for one another here: a loose mooring ring, a snag below the stage, a boat wanted for hire. Beneath them, three entries in different hands each record a boat overturned near the crossing. One lists grain, one lists hides and one names no cargo at all. Someone has chalked “Silverfin?” beside the last, and someone else has rubbed it out.

locations.name: West of Rillford
locations.description: Beyond Rillford’s ferry stage the river widens and runs on out of sight. Nobody here has marked where it goes. The ferry stage lies east.

locations.name: Towpath Willow Bank
locations.description: A worn towpath leaves the south road and follows the river’s north bank under leaning willows. Reedbed Approach is east; the towpath runs on west.

locations.name: Towpath Mooring Posts
locations.description: Old mooring posts stand along the bank, their tops grooved by rope. The water runs deep enough here to drop a line. The towpath runs east and west.

locations.name: Towpath Sedge Flats
locations.description: Sedge flats spread between the towpath and the water, cut by narrow channels. Something heavy has rooted along the margin. The towpath runs east and west.

locations.name: Towpath Culvert
locations.description: The towpath crosses a stone culvert where a field drain empties into the river. Fox tracks mark the mud at its mouth. The towpath runs east and west.

locations.name: Quay Lane
locations.description: The towpath widens into a cart lane between stacked crates and coiled rope. Voices and the knock of loading carry from the quay to the west. The towpath back toward Bellwold runs east.

locations.name: North Quay
locations.description: Boats nose against the stone quay while crews load, mend and argue over the current. The ferry stage reaches into the river to the south. The customs house is west, the guild hall is north, and the towpath to Bellwold runs east.

locations.name: Customs House
locations.description: Ledgers fill the shelves of a narrow stone office, and a counter faces the quay door. A notice is pinned beside the door. The quay is east; Warehouse Row lies west.

readables.label: Cargo notice
readables.description: A notice pinned beside the customs-house door.
readables.text: Cargo landed or loaded at the Rillford quay is to be declared at this house before it moves on. A declaration names the goods, their quantity, their owner and the boat or cart that carries them. The notice sets out no rates and says nothing about who may carry passengers.

npcs.name: Customs Clerk
npcs.description: A customs clerk copies a cargo declaration into a ledger, checking each line against the bill beside it.
npcs.activityDescription: copying cargo declarations into a ledger
npcs.greeting: “Declaring cargo? The notice by the door says what I need. Otherwise, mind the ledgers.”

topics.response: “Whatever comes off a boat or goes onto one gets written here: goods, quantity, owner, boat. That’s the job.”
“The Crown wants to know what moves through the crossing. Some merchants think that keeps things fair. Others think it’s our business only when it suits us.”
“I record cargo. If you want to talk money, talk to someone who can set it. I won’t quote you a number.”
“I record what boats declare. I’ve heard the crews’ stories like everyone else. None of them is in my ledger.”

dialogue.prompt: “Declaring cargo? The notice by the door says what I need. Otherwise, mind the ledgers.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “A clerk of the customs house. I write down what crosses the quay.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “Copying today’s declarations. Every line has to match the bill.”

choices.label: What is Rillford like?
choices.response: “Busy. Boats in, boats out, and everyone sure their cargo is the one that matters.”

choices.label: What does the cargo notice ask for?
choices.response: “Goods, quantity, owner, and the boat or cart carrying them. Bring me those and you’re done here.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I keep the declarations. Ask the guild or the crews about the rest.”

locations.name: Guild Hall
locations.description: Long tables hold bills of lading and a chalked board of boats due and boats gone. Merchants talk in low, quick voices. The quay is south; the inn is west.

npcs.name: Guildmistress Selda Rook
npcs.description: Selda Rook stands over a bill of lading at the long table, marking each cargo line before she signs.
npcs.activityDescription: checking bills of lading
npcs.greeting: “If you’ve business on the river, it starts with a record. What are you carrying?”

topics.response: “Agreed rules for loading, passage and disputes protect the small trader as much as the big house. Without them, whoever shouts loudest sets the terms.”
“The ferry guild wants exclusive rights. The independent boatmen say rules will become a fence. I want regulation, but I don’t speak for every merchant on this quay, and I won’t pretend to.”

“Crews say Old Silverfin has been overturning boats with certain cargoes. Which cargoes? Every account I hear is different. Until we write down what each boat carried and where it went over, I won’t name a cause.”
“Write down what was loaded, who loaded it and where the boat was bound. Then compare. A pattern you can check is worth more than a story you like.”
“The customs house wants the crossing legible to the Crown. Some here welcome that. Others don’t.”
“Bellwold’s goods come down the towpath and go out on our boats. Harrowfen’s grain moves through here too. When one place is short, the others hear about it.”

dialogue.prompt: “If you’ve business on the river, it starts with a record. What are you carrying?”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Selda Rook. I speak for the merchants who want river commerce run by agreed rules. Not all of them, mind.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “Checking bills of lading. If a boat goes over, I want to know what it carried before anyone tells me why.”

choices.label: What is Rillford like?
choices.response: “A crossing town. Warehouses, customs, a livestock market each week, and more opinions about the river than boats on it.”

choices.label: What is the ferry dispute?
choices.response: “The ferry guild wants exclusive rights to carry across. The independent boatmen think that would shut them out. I support regulation, and I know not everyone trusts the people who’d write it.”

choices.label: What about Old Silverfin?
choices.response: “Some crews call it a warning. Some blame poor loading, and some think someone wants boats to sink. I want the cargoes written down before anyone decides.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Ask me about the river trade, the guild or the crossing.”

locations.name: Quayside Inn
locations.description: Crews and carters share the benches of a low, smoky common room. Wet coats steam by the hearth. The guild hall is east; the livestock market is west.

locations.name: Warehouse Row
locations.description: Timber warehouses stand shoulder to shoulder, their doors open on sacks, bales and barrels. Boat crews mend gear between loads. The customs house is east; the livestock market is north.

npcs.name: Independent Boatman
npcs.description: A boatman sits on an upturned hull, splicing a rope end and keeping half an eye on the warehouse doors.
npcs.activityDescription: splicing rope between loads
npcs.greeting: “If you’re from the guild, I’ve said my piece. If not, sit down.”

topics.response: “The guild calls it regulation. To me it looks like a fence round the river with their name on the gate. Rules written by the biggest boats tend to suit the biggest boats.”
“Some crews say it’s a warning. Some say it’s bad loading. A few reckon someone’s tipping boats on purpose to settle the ferry fight. I’ve not seen it myself, so I won’t tell you which.”
“Crossing’s arranged boat by boat. Nobody’s carrying passengers off this quay just now.”
“Watch the current, not the stories. It changes with the weather, and it doesn’t care who holds the rights.”

dialogue.prompt: “If you’re from the guild, I’ve said my piece. If not, sit down.”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “I work my own boat. No guild, no exclusive rights, and I’d like to keep it that way.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “Splicing rope. A frayed line costs more than a slow afternoon.”

choices.label: What is Rillford like?
choices.response: “Good water, crowded quay, and everyone arguing over who gets to carry what.”

choices.label: Can you take me across?
choices.response: “Not from here, not now. Who carries whom across is half of what the guild fight is about.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “I know boats and this stretch of water. Ask about those.”

locations.name: Livestock Market
locations.description: Hurdle pens fill the open ground. The weekly market leaves trampled straw and the smell of animals long after it ends. The inn is east; Warehouse Row is south.

locations.name: South Landing
locations.description: A muddy landing on the south bank faces the ferry stage across the water. Boats put in here when the crews are carrying, but none waits now. A lane runs south.

locations.name: South Lane
locations.description: Low cottages and net sheds line a lane along Rillford’s south bank. The landing is north; a track leads east toward Bellwold’s Milepost Workshop.

locations.name: Landing Lane
locations.description: The track firms into a lane as it nears the river. Rillford’s roofs show to the west; the sedge track runs east.

locations.name: Sedge Track
locations.description: A narrow track runs through sedge and alder scrub. The Milepost Workshop is east; the track continues west toward Rillford.

locations.name: Far Bank Track
locations.description: The road climbs away from the bridge onto firmer ground. Lower Rill Bridge is north; the old mile marker is south.

locations.name: Old South Mile Marker
locations.description: A weathered stone marker stands beside the packed road. Most of its face is worn smooth; shallow grooves remain beneath the lichen. Far Bank Track is north; the unfinished road lies south, and a dirt track branches west.

readables.label: Mile marker inscription
readables.description: A shallow inscription cut into the marker face.
readables.text: The surviving inscription records a distance from Bellwold. Its destination name has worn away.

locations.name: Mile Marker West Track
locations.description: The packed dirt bends west from the stone marker. Dry grass rasps against your boots, and a line of hazel leaves shivers ahead; the marker is east.

locations.name: Hazel Cut
locations.description: Hazel branches narrow the track, their leaves whispering over the road. A faint smell of woodsmoke drifts from the west; the Mile Marker West Track is east.

locations.name: Milepost Workshop
locations.description: Pale shavings curl across a scarred workbench beside a low, warm stove. A file rasps against metal; the hazel track runs east, and a sedge-lined track leads west toward Rillford’s south landing.

npcs.name: Nessa Rill
npcs.description: Nessa braces a cartwheel against a low stand, pale shavings clinging to her sleeves as she checks its rim for a wobble.
npcs.activityDescription: truing a cartwheel against a wooden brace
npcs.greeting: “Mind the shavings; they gather thick around the bench. What brings you this way?”

topics.response: “I’m Nessa Rill. I live in the loft above the bench and mend carts, handles, and wooden fittings.”
“The track ends here. Wagons can turn around by the bench; beyond the hazel there is no road I can send you along.”

dialogue.prompt: “Mind the shavings; they gather thick around the bench. What brings you this way?”

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.response: “Nessa Rill. I live in the loft above the bench and make my living repairing carts, handles, and wooden fittings.”

choices.label: What are you doing?
choices.response: “I’m truing this cartwheel. The rim was loose enough to send a load skidding if I left it.”

choices.label: What is Bellwold like?
choices.response: “Bellwold is the nearest place to trade and see familiar faces. I go in when I need supplies or news.”

choices.label: What do you repair?
choices.response: “Mostly cart wheels, handles, and wooden fittings. If the break is metal, I send folks to Darric at the forge.”

choices.label: Why set up here?
choices.response: “The old road brings wagons past my door, and the loft keeps me close to the work. It suits me.”

npcs.unknownTopicResponse: “Ask me about the repair work or the road. I’m better with a spoke than a rumor.”

locations.name: Unfinished South Road
locations.description: The packed road ends at a shallow cut in the earth. Loose soil and ungraded ground extend beyond it, with no roofs visible. The old mile marker is north.

locations.name: Old Bell Tower Road
locations.description: The road climbs north, and Bellwold’s roofs drop from view behind a rise. The old tower’s outline stands against the sky. A narrow track branches east, where water glints beside the mill.

locations.name: Old Bell Tower
locations.description: Dust gathers in the seams between the stones. A bronze bell hangs motionless in a weathered frame; its clapper rests against its side.

readables.label: Tower inscription
readables.description: A weathered inscription at the tower entrance.
readables.text: A copied account says the bell was heard before storms. It also records the period when seventeen villagers disappeared while the bell sounded continuously. The account does not explain what connected those events, or why the bell later fell silent.

locations.name: Abandoned Watermill
locations.description: The air by the channel is damp and cool. A slow wooden creak carries from the wheel, and water glints through the channel. A damp work ledger lies open on the desk. The tower road is west; the east track follows the channel.

readables.label: Mill work ledger
readables.description: A damp ledger left on the mill desk.
readables.text: The last entries record the mill wheel moving on nights when the channel ran low. The writer notes the dates, water level, and movement, but gives no explanation.

takeables.label: Copper Axe
takeables.description: A copper axe with a worn handle and a serviceable edge, suitable for chopping wood.
takeables.roomDescription: A copper axe leans against the wall.

locations.name: East Mill Track
locations.description: The road leaves the mill and runs east between shallow drainage channels. The abandoned watermill is west; a bend in the track lies east.

locations.name: East Road Bend
locations.description: The packed track curves around a low rise; the mill channel has vanished from view. A narrower path branches north toward the old church. East Mill Track is west; the road verge is east.

locations.name: North Church Track
locations.description: A narrow track climbs north between low banks of grass. Wind combs the grass as the road rises; East Road Bend is south and the church approach is north.

locations.name: Church Approach
locations.description: The track opens into bare ground before a dark timber doorway. Wind pushes dry leaves across the clearing; the entrance is north and the road returns south.

locations.name: Abandoned Church
locations.description: Dust powders the stone floor, and muted light falls through gaps in the roof. A narrow stair climbs toward a frame overhead; worn steps descend below.

locations.name: Church Belfry
locations.description: Wind cuts through the narrow belfry. A weathered frame hangs over the roofline, ringed by empty mounting holes; a cut length of rope taps against it. The stair leads down to the nave.

locations.name: Church Annex
locations.description: The steps descend into a low stone room. Damp darkens the mortar, and shallow shelves run along the walls. A locked iron door stands to the east; the stair leads up.

interactables.label: Iron door
interactables.description: A heavy iron door is set into the eastern wall. A narrow keyhole is worn smooth around its edge.

itemUses.response: The old church key turns with a dry click. The iron door opens onto a low corridor descending beneath the annex.
itemUses.repeatResponse: The iron door stands open. The old key still turns in its lock.

locations.name: Undercrypt Entry
locations.description: A low stone corridor begins beyond the iron door. Damp air carries the smell of earth; a shallow recess opens east, the passage runs north, and the annex lies west.

locations.name: Entry Recess
locations.description: The eastern recess ends at bare stone. A smooth layer of dust covers the floor; the corridor returns west.

locations.name: First Passage
locations.description: Rough stone presses close on either side, leaving space for two people to pass. Footsteps echo toward a fork north; the entry lies south.

locations.name: Three-Way Fork
locations.description: Three worn corridors meet beneath a cracked arch. Fine grit crunches underfoot; the first passage is south, the central hall north, and narrow branches open east and west.

locations.name: Blind Passage
locations.description: The western branch stops at a rough stone wall; loose grit gathers at its base. The fork lies east.

locations.name: Eastern Bend
locations.description: Stone walls curve north, where a colder draft threads through the passage. The fork lies west.

locations.name: Eastern Corridor
locations.description: Bootsteps echo down the straight corridor. The central hall opens west, the passage returns south, and a short branch ends east.

locations.name: Eastern Dead End
locations.description: The eastern corridor ends at a collapsed stone niche; fine dust lies undisturbed across the floor. The corridor is west.

locations.name: Central Hall
locations.description: A square chamber gathers the echoes of four passages. Cold air spills from the northern route; the fork lies south, with cross-corridors west and east.

locations.name: Western Corridor
locations.description: A narrow passage runs west from the central hall; a stone shelf juts from the northern wall into a shallow recess.

locations.name: Western Burial Recess
locations.description: A stone shelf juts from the wall of this shallow recess; dust gathers along its edge. The passage returns south.

locations.name: Northern Passage
locations.description: Cool air brushes through the straight passage. The central hall lies south; a larger junction waits north.

locations.name: Upper Junction
locations.description: Stone branches meet beneath an old lintel. Dust shifts in a draft; the northern passage is south, recesses open east and west, and a narrow route continues north.

locations.name: West Burial Recess
locations.description: A narrow stone shelf projects from the western wall, its surface dulled by dust. The junction lies east.

locations.name: East Burial Recess
locations.description: A cracked stone slab rests in the small recess, its surface scored with pale lines. The junction lies west.

locations.name: Reliquary Approach
locations.description: A squared arch rises ahead; cool, still air flows from a chamber to the north. The upper junction lies south.

locations.name: Church Reliquary
locations.description: Dry, still air hangs in the chamber. A narrow sword rests on a black stone shelf beneath a faded carving of a watchful hand.

takeables.label: Reliquary sword
takeables.description: A carefully balanced steel sword with a narrow fuller. Its workmanship grants +2 attack power when equipped.
takeables.roomDescription: The reliquary sword rests on the black stone shelf.

locations.name: Eastern Road Verge
locations.description: The packed track ends at open ground beyond the bend. Grass pushes through the wheel ruts, and the eastern way is overgrown. The bend lies west.

locationGroups.name: Bellwold
locationGroups.description: A growing trading settlement near the frontier of the Crown of Heskar. Its exact legal status is not established.

locationGroups.name: Harrowfen
locationGroups.description: A farming village of low fields and drainage cuts, half a day west of Bellwold. Much of its land belongs to Heskar noble families.

locationGroups.name: Rillford
locationGroups.description: A river crossing and trading town a day southwest of Bellwold along the Lower Rill, with a contested ferry trade.

locationGroups.name: Lower Rill
locationGroups.description: A provisional name for the river passing near Bellwold. Its full course is not recorded.

quests.title: The Mill Ledger
quests.summary: Read the abandoned watermill’s work ledger and report its recorded observations to Anwen. The record does not establish why the wheel moved.

objectives.label: Read the work ledger at the abandoned watermill

quests.title: The Church Reliquary
quests.summary: Find the old church key in the Old Grain House, open the annex beneath the abandoned church, and recover the reliquary sword. Return it to Anwen for 20 gold; she will inspect it and return the same blade to you.

objectives.label: Find the old church key behind the Old Grain House tally cabinet
Unlock the iron door in the church annex
Recover the reliquary sword from the undercrypt

quests.title: A Measure Between Towns
quests.summary: Read Anwen Marr’s scale note in Bellwold and Harrowfen’s yield tallies, then help Reeve Maela choose how a future grain handoff will be recorded. Neither record establishes why the yields have fallen.

objectives.label: Read Anwen Marr’s scale note in Bellwold
Read Harrowfen’s yield tallies at the weigh-house

branches.label: Compare the records
branches.summary: Read the two records before recommending how future grain handoffs should be recorded.

woodcuttingTrees.logDescription: A bundled set of fresh pine logs, still carrying a sharp resin scent.
